002_h1: UAE Youth Social Innovation Workshop Series
003_p: Six months in which young people turned something they cared about into a social enterprise prototype — through seriously playful investigation.
017_alt: The full cohort of 38 young participants and facilitators at Sheraa, Sharjah
018_figcaption: The cohort at Sheraa, Sharjah — young people from across the UAE.
019_p: Over six months, in partnership with Sheraa, 38 young people across the UAE registered to turn something they cared about into a real social enterprise. About twenty saw it through to the end.
020_p: Not by lecture. They worked through a series of workshops rooted in the ME=WE framework and supported by systems thinking, design thinking, and appreciative inquiry — exploring their own identity, their relationships with self, society, and service, and where passion meets purpose.
021_p: Then they went out. Deep listening and conversations in their own communities came first — need-finding before ideas — then shaping what they heard into something, then testing it again and again with the people they hoped to serve. Most ideas changed several times before they held.
022_p: The support around them was its own lesson. INNOCO facilitators, like-minded individuals, and organizations gave their knowledge, expertise, and in-kind services freely, with no expectation of return.
023_p: What came out of it wasn’t a set of assignments.
024_span: It was real prototypes, real pitches, and a group of young people who discovered they could build something.
